import sys

def main():
    s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
    n = len(s)
    res = s[0] if n > 0 else ""
    i = 1
    flag = 0  # indicates whether we have already replaced "at"
    while i < n:
        # Check for "at" replacement (only once, and not near the end)
        if flag == 0 and i < n - 2:
            if s[i:i+2] == "at":
                res += '@'
                i += 2
                flag = 1
                continue
        # Check for "dot" replacement (anywhere, but not near the end)
        if i < n - 3:
            if s[i:i+3] == "dot":
                res += '.'
                i += 3
                continue
        # Otherwise, add the current character
        res += s[i]
        i += 1
    print(res)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
